definitions.text: Explain the relationship between zero net force and constant velocity.

components.text: Explain the relationship between zero net force and constant velocity.

messages.content: What happens to the velocity of a moving object when its net force is zero?
Zero net force means zero acceleration, so its velocity remains constant.
For the same object with zero net force and no friction, what happens as more time passes?
It slows to rest even though the net force remains zero; a continuing forward force is necessary to maintain its velocity.

response.reason: The learner initially gives the correct force–acceleration–velocity relationship, but then explicitly contradicts it for the same zero-net-force conditions. This unresolved conceptual error prevents support for either criterion.
response.nextEvidenceObjective: Ask the learner to reconcile their two statements by explaining whether velocity changes over time when net force stays zero, why, and when the zero-net-force relationship can be used.

judgments.reason: The initial causal explanation is correct, but the later claim that an object slows with zero net force and requires a continuing force to maintain velocity is a direct, unresolved error under comparable conditions.
